stories.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO, Harvey Jones board chair

key_facts.fact: Nvidia's board announced on November 12, 2026 that Jensen Huang resigned as President, CEO and board member, effective immediately; CFO Colette Kress agreed to serve as interim CEO while remaining CFO.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) Board of Directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately. Colette Kress... has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer.

key_facts.fact: Harvey C. Jones was appointed the first-ever Chair of Nvidia's board, and the board is searching for a permanent CEO among internal and external candidates.
key_facts.excerpt: Harvey C. Jones Appointed First-Ever Chair of the Board... The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates.

key_facts.fact: Per Nvidia's 8-K filing, the board accepted Huang's resignation on November 11, 2026; Kress, 59, has been CFO since 2013.
key_facts.excerpt: On November 11, 2026, the Board of Directors... accepted the resignation of Jen-Hsun Huang... the Board appointed NVIDIA's Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Colette M. Kress, age 59, to serve as interim Chief Executive Officer

key_facts.fact: Huang stepped down days after admitting to an affair with a woman US authorities suspect of being a Chinese spy, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed.
key_facts.excerpt: just a few days after he admitted to a romantic affair with an alleged Chinese spy, sparking a U.S. national security crisis.

key_facts.fact: In her first staff email, Kress called it 'an extraordinarily difficult period' and set a company meeting for November 18 at 9am PT.
key_facts.excerpt: The Board, Estaff and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period... we will host a company meeting on November 18 at 9am PT.

key_facts.fact: President Trump posted on Truth Social that Apple executive chairman Tim Cook is the 'only one man' to replace Huang: 'A Legend replaces a Legend!'
key_facts.excerpt: In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that "only one man" could take Huang's place: Tim Cook of Apple. "A Legend replaces a Legend!" he wrote.

key_facts.fact: Trump said on Stephen A. Smith's podcast that Huang called him and is 'going through hell', and that Huang should have stepped down only if the woman was a spy, which he said has not been determined.
key_facts.excerpt: the big thing is, was the woman a spy, and I don't know if that's been determined yet... I spoke to him yesterday. He's going through hell.

stories.headline: Congress summons Huang and Lutnick to testify on Nvidia; White House weighs Lutnick's future

key_facts.fact: Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott sent letters on Thursday asking Jensen Huang to testify on December 3 and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on December 10, threatening subpoenas if they decline.
key_facts.excerpt: In the letters, Scott asked that Huang and Lutnick voluntarily appear before the Senate Banking Committee to testify Dec. 3 and Dec. 10, respectively.

key_facts.fact: A Commerce spokesperson said Lutnick 'has proactively agreed to appear voluntarily' before the Banking Committee.
key_facts.excerpt: "Secretary Lutnick has proactively agreed to appear voluntarily before the Banking Committee to address their questions," Kristen Eichamer, a spokesperson for Lutnick, told NBC News.

key_facts.fact: House Foreign Affairs Chair Brian Mast asked Huang for a closed-door transcribed interview on December 1, with a subpoena if he did not confirm by Friday evening.
key_facts.excerpt: Mast asked that he appear before the committee Dec. 1 for a "closed-door, transcribed interview," adding that a subpoena would be issued if Huang did not confirm the interview by Friday evening.

key_facts.fact: Three House committees also asked Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter to appear, and summoned Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler for a December 3 hearing.
key_facts.excerpt: Three other House committees have asked Huang and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter to appear for separate hearings on December 1 and 2, or face subpoenas. Under Secretary of Commerce Jeffrey Kessler was summoned for a December 3 hearing.

key_facts.fact: Reuters reported senior White House officials are discussing whether Lutnick should be pushed out, as lawmakers criticize Commerce for not adding Chinese companies to the Entity List; the US has posted no additions since October 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Senior White House officials are discussing whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick should be pushed out amid a spy scandal surrounding Nvidia's now-former CEO Jensen Huang... The U.S. has not posted any additions to that list since October 2025

key_facts.fact: A White House official said Trump 'maintains complete confidence' in Lutnick.
key_facts.excerpt: "President Trump maintains complete confidence in the secretary and his ability to carry out the position as the most transformative Commerce Secretary in modern history."

key_facts.fact: Megaspeed, the Singapore company whose executive Alice Huang is suspected of spying, has bought more than $4.8 billion in advanced Nvidia AI chips since June 2024, per senators Warren and Coons.
key_facts.excerpt: Alice Huang, an executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that has purchased more than $4.8 billion in advanced Nvidia AI chips since June 2024.

stories.headline: SpaceX plans $74B in AI supercomputing campuses in Arizona ($50B) and Texas ($24B)

key_facts.fact: SpaceX announced on November 12 more than $74 billion in planned investment in two supercompute facilities: up to $24 billion at Starbase in Texas and roughly $50 billion in Cochise County, Arizona.
key_facts.excerpt: a major new supercompute facility at Starbase in the Rio Grande Valley in Texas, and a second campus in Cochise County, Arizona. Together, they represent more than $74 billion in planned American investment

key_facts.fact: The Texas facility will generate its own electricity rather than draw from the public grid; SpaceX also committed $220 million to expand Brownsville's water and wastewater infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: The facility will generate its own electricity without drawing power from the public grid. We're also committing $220 million to expand Brownsville's water and wastewater infrastructure

key_facts.fact: The Texas site sits on 444 acres near Starbase, and the Arizona project still requires county approval; it is projected to create 5,500 construction and 1,000 permanent jobs.
key_facts.excerpt: In Texas, SpaceX plans to invest $24 billion in a data center campus on 444 acres of company-owned land near the Starbase rocket site... The Arizona project still requires approval from the county.

key_facts.fact: The Arizona plan includes a proposed $3.6 billion investment in electrical infrastructure and a 24-gigawatt-hour battery storage system; a petition opposing it has about 2,400 signatures.
key_facts.excerpt: The project also includes a proposed $3.6 billion investment in electrical infrastructure and a 24-gigawatt-hour battery storage system... a petition opposing the project has gathered approximately 2,400 signatures

key_facts.fact: The Texas campus includes a gas-fired power plant that SpaceX would build, own and operate.
key_facts.excerpt: The $74 billion worth of infrastructure projects includes constructing, owning and operating a gas-fired power plant at the Texas site

key_facts.fact: The announcement came less than a week after Brownsville's city commission approved a 90-day moratorium on data center development; the land was deannexed by Brownsville and annexed by Starbase.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX's announcement comes less than a week after the Brownsville City Commission unanimously approved a 90-day moratorium on data center development in the city.

stories.headline: Nscale's amended IPO filing shows $5.5B debt, $1.69B nine-month loss and deeper Nvidia ties

key_facts.fact: Nscale filed Amendment No. 1 to its S-1 on November 12, 2026, showing estimated total debt of $5.52 billion as of September 30, up from $78.9 million at end-2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Total debt, including current portion | $5,516.3 | $78.9

key_facts.fact: Nine-month revenue was an estimated $307.5 million versus $21.3 million a year earlier, with a net loss of $1.69 billion versus $433.3 million.
Debt had been $137.4 million at the end of June; Nvidia committed $2 billion of the more than $3 billion in convertible financing agreed in September, versus $1 billion in the first filing.
key_facts.excerpt: At the end of June it was $137.4m... Nvidia committed $2bn of the more than $3bn in convertible financing Nscale agreed in September... The first filing disclosed only $1bn

key_facts.fact: A separate $1 billion 'NVIDIA Sale' of convertible notes or non-voting shares is set to close on or around November 16, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: a further $1.0 billion of unsecured convertible loan notes or Non-Voting Shares (as applicable) that will be issued to NVIDIA (the "NVIDIA Sale")... The NVIDIA Sale will close on or around November 16, 2026.

key_facts.fact: The London-based neocloud, which filed to list on the NYSE in September, did not specify how much it intends to raise.
key_facts.excerpt: London-based Nscale filed to go public in September, but hasn't updated its prospectus since then. The company did not specify how much it intends to raise in the public offering on the New York Stock Exchange.

key_facts.fact: Nscale wrote that Nvidia is not obliged to give it priority allocation, favorable pricing or early access to new products.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia is not obliged to "give us priority allocation, favorable pricing or early access to new products", Nscale wrote, according to Bloomberg.

stories.headline: Samsung in talks to buy data center cooling maker Modine; shares jump 28% after hours

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics is in talks to acquire Modine Manufacturing, a maker of data center cooling systems, in a deal that could come together in the coming weeks, Bloomberg reported on November 12.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics Co. is in talks to acquire Modine Manufacturing Co., a maker of cooling systems for data centers... could come together as soon as the coming weeks

key_facts.fact: Modine closed at $106.10, a market value of about $5.6 billion, then jumped about 28% to above $135 in late trading; both companies declined to comment.
key_facts.excerpt: Modine closed regular trading at $106.10, a market value of about $5.6B, then soared past $135 in late trading, a 28% jump.

key_facts.fact: Modine's data center segment revenue rose 95% year over year to $439.7 million in its latest quarter; it projects fiscal 2027 revenue of up to $3.2 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Third-quarter revenue in its data center segment rose 95% from a year earlier to $439.7 million... Revenue for fiscal 2027 (April 2026 to March 2027) is projected at up to $3.2 billion

key_facts.fact: Seoul Economic Daily estimates a full takeover at $7.5-8 billion, which would exceed the roughly $8 billion Samsung paid for Harman in 2017 if above that level.
key_facts.excerpt: the expected acquisition price is estimated at $7.5 billion to $8 billion... If the price exceeds the roughly $8 billion Samsung paid for Harman in 2017, the deal could become the largest merger and acquisition in Samsung Electronics' history.

key_facts.fact: Samsung bought German cooling specialist FläktGroup for €1.5 billion last year; Modine spun off its automotive business in October to become a pure-play thermal-management company.
key_facts.excerpt: The company bought Germany's FläktGroup, another cooling specialist, for €1.5B last year... in October it spun off its automotive business to become a pure-play thermal-management company.

stories.headline: Cerebras beats Q3 estimates, raises 2026 outlook and signs Microsoft as third hyperscaler

key_facts.fact: Cerebras reported record Q3 core revenue of $230.9 million, up 70% year over year, versus the $214.7 million LSEG consensus; GAAP revenue was $210.8 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Record GAAP revenue of $210.8 million - Record Core revenue of $230.9 million

key_facts.fact: Core cloud and other services revenue rose 272% to $144.9 million, and Cerebras has 700 megawatts of data center capacity under contract.
key_facts.excerpt: Core cloud and other services revenue: $144.9 million, up 272% year-over-year... 700 megawatts of data center capacity now under contract

key_facts.fact: Q4 guidance is $310-330 million in core revenue; full-year 2026 core revenue guidance is $940-960 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Core revenue of approximately $310 to $330 million... Core revenue of $940 to $960 million

key_facts.fact: CEO Andrew Feldman named Microsoft as the new 'top three hyperscaler' customer, said it signed in October and that revenue begins in Q1 2027; it joins AWS and Oracle.
key_facts.excerpt: "We believe revenue begins to show up in Q1 '27," Feldman said in the interview, adding that Microsoft signed the deal in October. Cerebras has also landed deals with other major cloud providers Amazon and Oracle.

key_facts.fact: Shares rose almost 18% in late trading after the report.
key_facts.excerpt: announcing a new deal with Microsoft Corp., sending its stock up almost 18% in late trading.

key_facts.fact: Cerebras reported $26.1 billion in remaining performance obligations; Reuters reported the backlog is underpinned by its OpenAI computing deal.
key_facts.excerpt: Cerebras reported $26.1 billion in remaining performance obligations... Reuters reported that the backlog is underpinned by Cerebras' deal to supply computing power to OpenAI

stories.headline: Applied Materials posts record $10.4B quarter, sees chip-equipment demand up 30%+ in 2027

key_facts.fact: Applied Materials reported record fiscal Q4 revenue of $10.41 billion, up 53% year over year, and record non-GAAP EPS of $4.16, up 92%.
key_facts.excerpt: Record quarterly revenue $10.41 billion, up 53 percent year over year... record non-GAAP EPS $4.16, up 43 percent and 92 percent year over year

key_facts.fact: Fiscal 2026 revenue was a record $34.45 billion, up 21%.
key_facts.excerpt: Record annual revenue $34.45 billion, up 21 percent year over year

key_facts.fact: It guided fiscal Q1 2027 revenue to $11.1 billion plus or minus $500 million and non-GAAP EPS of $4.35 plus or minus $0.20, in a 14-week quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: Total revenue | $ | 11,100 | +/- | $ | 500 | Non-GAAP diluted EPS | $ | 4.35 | +/- | $ | 0.20

key_facts.fact: CEO Gary Dickerson said wafer fab equipment demand will rise more than 30% in 2027, and that customers are asking to accelerate deliveries.
key_facts.excerpt: The semiconductor equipment maker expects wafer fab equipment demand to rise more than 30% in 2027... "Nobody is saying that they're not wanting the tools as fast as we can get them," Dickerson said

key_facts.fact: Semiconductor Systems revenue reached $8 billion, up 64%, with record DRAM and advanced packaging sales; leading-edge logic and DRAM fabs are running at full utilization.
key_facts.excerpt: Semiconductor Systems revenue reached $8 billion in the fourth quarter, up 64% year over year... Hill said leading-edge logic and DRAM fabrication plants are running at full utilization.

key_facts.fact: Applied plans to double systems output from Q4 2026 levels by 2028 and expects China to be under 25% of its business in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is investing to double systems output from fourth-quarter 2026 levels by 2028... Hill expects China shipments to account for less than 25% of Applied Materials' business in 2027
